text: Mohamed Abdelaziz Dja'it (1886–1970) (Arabic: محمد عبد العزيز جعيط) was an Islamic scholar who served as Mufti of the Republic of Tunisia from 1957 to 1960. He was born in 1886 during the French protectorate of Tunisia and was the son of Youssef Djaït, who served as Prime Minister under the Beylik of Tunis. In the early years of Tunisian independence, President Habib Bourguiba referenced Dja'it's 1949 majalla publication when justifying the new Code of Personal Status, which included laws on family life and women's status, from a religious perspective. Dja'it issued a fatwa opposing the code in September 1956 but later withdrew his opposition and was appointed Mufti of the Republic. He was eventually dismissed for criticizing Bourguiba's position on fasting.
